35: #  error "BK7258 OpenVela SMP requires the fixed 480 MHz CP contract"
36: #endif
37: 
38: #define BK7258_CPU2_ONLINE_CYCLES  (CONFIG_BK7258_CPU_FREQ_HZ / 2u)
39: #define BK7258_CPU2_POLL_LIMIT     4000000u
40: 
41: extern uint8_t __secondary_vectors_start[];
42: extern uint8_t __secondary_boot_stack_base[];
43: 
44: static void bk7258_cpu2_hold_reset(void)
45: {
46:   putreg32(getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL) & ~BK7258_CPU2_RESET_RELEASE,
47:            BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL);
48:   UP_DSB();
49: }
50: 
51: static void bk7258_cpu2_release_reset(void)
52: {
53:   putreg32(getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL) | BK7258_CPU2_RESET_RELEASE,
54:            BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL);
55:   UP_DSB();
56:   __asm__ volatile("sev" ::: "memory");
57: }
58: 
59: static void __attribute__((used, noreturn)) bk7258_secondary_idle(void)
60: {
61:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_IDLE);
62:   arm_initialize_stack();
63:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_STACK);
64:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_ONLINE);
65:   bk7258_smp_boot_notify();
66:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_NOTIFY);
67:   up_irq_enable();
68:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_IRQ_ON);
69:   sched_note_cpu_started(this_task());
70:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_SCHED);
71:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_WAIT);
72:   nx_idle_trampoline();
73:   PANIC();
74: }
75: 
76: static void __attribute__((naked, noreturn))
77: bk7258_secondary_enter(uintptr_t idle_top __attribute__((unused)),
78:                        uintptr_t idle_base __attribute__((unused)))
79: {
80:   __asm__ volatile
81:     (
82:       "msr psp, r0\n"
83: #ifdef CONFIG_ARMV8M_STACKCHECK_HARDWARE
84:       "msr psplim, r1\n"
85: #endif
86:       "mrs r1, control\n"
87:       "orr r1, r1, #2\n"
88:       "msr control, r1\n"
89:       "isb sy\n"
90:       "b bk7258_secondary_idle\n"
91:     );
92: }
93: 
94: static void __attribute__((used, noinline, noreturn,
95:                            target("general-regs-only")))
96: bk7258_secondary_boot(void)
97: {
98:   struct tcb_s *tcb;
99:   uintptr_t idle_top;
100: 
101:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_ENTRY);
102:   bk7258_cpu_private_initialize(false);
103:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_PRIVATE);
104:   bk7258_irqinitialize_secondary();
105:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_IRQ);
106:   if (bk7258_mbox_secondary_init() < 0)
107:     {
108:       PANIC();
109:     }
110: 
111:   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX);
112: 
113:   tcb = current_task(1);
114:   idle_top = ((uintptr_t)tcb->stack_base_ptr + tcb->adj_stack_size) & ~7u;
115:   bk7258_secondary_enter(idle_top, (uintptr_t)tcb->stack_base_ptr);
116: }
117: 
118: void __attribute__((naked, noreturn, section(".start_text")))
119: bk7258_secondary_start(void)
120: {
121:   __asm__ volatile
122:     (
123:       "cpsid i\n"
124:       "movs r0, #1\n"
125:       "ldr r1, =0x20000000\n"
126:       "str r0, [r1]\n"
127:       "ldr r0, =__secondary_boot_stack_base\n"
128:       "msr msplim, r0\n"
129:       "b bk7258_secondary_boot\n"
130:     );
131: }
132: 
133: int up_cpu_start(int cpu)
134: {
135:   irqstate_t flags;
136:   uint32_t started;
137:   uint32_t polls = 0;
138:   uint32_t control;
139:   uint32_t status;
140:   bool ping_sent = false;
141: 
142:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_ENTER);
143: 
144:   if (cpu != 1 || this_cpu() != 0)
145:     {
146:       return -EINVAL;
147:     }
148: 
149:   status = getreg32(BK7258_CPU_RUN_STATUS);
150:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(0, status);
151:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(1, bk7258_mbox_smp_ready());
152:   if ((status & BK7258_CPU_STATUS_CPU2_POWER_DOWN) != 0 ||
153:       !bk7258_mbox_smp_ready())
154:     {
155:       syslog(LOG_ERR, "CPU2 prerequisite failed: status=%08lx mbox=%u\n",
156:              (unsigned long)status, bk7258_mbox_smp_ready());
157:       PANIC();
158:     }
159: 
160:   bk7258_cpu2_hold_reset();
161:   control = getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL);
162:   status = getreg32(BK7258_CPU_RUN_STATUS);
163:   if ((control & BK7258_CPU2_RESET_RELEASE) != 0 ||
164:       (status & BK7258_CPU_STATUS_CPU2_RESET) != 0)
165:     {
166:       syslog(LOG_ERR, "CPU2 reset hold failed: ctrl=%08lx status=%08lx\n",
167:              (unsigned long)control, (unsigned long)status);
168:       PANIC();
169:     }
170: 
171:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_HELD);
172:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(0, control);
173:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(1, status);
174: 
175:   bk7258_smp_prepare_boot();
176:   putreg32(0, BK7258_CPU2_IRQ_EN0);
177:   putreg32(0, BK7258_CPU2_IRQ_EN1);
178:   modifyreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL, BK7258_CPU2_OFFSET_MASK,
179:               BK7258_CPU2_RXEVT_SEL |
180:               (((uintptr_t)__secondary_vectors_start >> 8) <<
181:                BK7258_CPU2_OFFSET_SHIFT));
182:   UP_DMB();
183:   UP_DSB();
184: 
185:   putreg32(getreg32(NVIC_DEMCR) | NVIC_DEMCR_TRCENA, NVIC_DEMCR);
186:   putreg32(0, DWT_CYCCNT);
187:   putreg32(getreg32(DWT_CTRL) | DWT_CTRL_CYCCNTENA_MASK, DWT_CTRL);
188:   started = getreg32(DWT_CYCCNT);
189:   flags = up_irq_save();
190:   bk7258_cpu2_release_reset();
191:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_RELEASED);
192:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(0, getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL));
193:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(1, getreg32(BK7258_CPU_RUN_STATUS));
194: 
195:   while (!bk7258_smp_boot_test_complete())
196:     {
197:       bk7258_mbox_kick_rx();
198:       if (bk7258_smp_boot_notified() && !ping_sent)
199:         {
200:           if (bk7258_smp_boot_ping(1) < 0)
201:             {
202:               break;
203:             }
204: 
205:           ping_sent = true;
206:           bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_ONLINE);
207:         }
208: 
209:       if (getreg32(DWT_CYCCNT) - started >= BK7258_CPU2_ONLINE_CYCLES ||
210:           ++polls >= BK7258_CPU2_POLL_LIMIT)
211:         {
212:           break;
213:         }
214:     }
215: 
216:   if (!bk7258_smp_boot_test_complete())
217:     {
218:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(0, getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL));
219:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(1, getreg32(BK7258_CPU_RUN_STATUS));
220:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(2, getreg32(BK7258_MBOX_CH1_STATUS));
221:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(3, getreg32(BK7258_MBOX_CH2_STATUS));
222:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(4, ping_sent);
223:       bk7258_cpu2_hold_reset();
224:       up_irq_restore(flags);
225:       syslog(LOG_ERR,
226:              "CPU2 online timeout: ctrl=%08lx status=%08lx fifo=%08lx/%08lx ping=%u\n",
227:              (unsigned long)getreg32(BK7258_CPU2_CONTROL),
228:              (unsigned long)getreg32(BK7258_CPU_RUN_STATUS),
229:              (unsigned long)getreg32(BK7258_MBOX_CH1_STATUS),
230:              (unsigned long)getreg32(BK7258_MBOX_CH2_STATUS), ping_sent);
231:       PANIC();
232:     }
233: 
234:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_IPI_DONE);
235:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(2, UINT32_MAX);
236:   putreg32(1u << (BK7258_EXTIRQ_MAILBOX & 31),
237:            NVIC_IRQ_CLRPEND(BK7258_EXTIRQ_MAILBOX));
238:   UP_DSB();
239:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_IRQ_RESTORE);
240:   up_irq_restore(flags);
241:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_IRQ_RETURN);
242:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_START_DONE);
243:   return OK;
244: }

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * BK7258 raw Mailbox SMP IPI.
3:  ****************************************************************************/
4: 
5: #include <nuttx/config.h>
6: 
7: #include <assert.h>
8: #include <errno.h>
9: #include <stdint.h>
10: #include <strings.h>
11: 
12: #include <nuttx/arch.h>
13: #include <nuttx/atomic.h>
14: #include <nuttx/sched.h>
15: 
16: #include "arm_internal.h"
17: #include "sched/sched.h"
18: #include "hardware/bk7258_mbox.h"
19: #include "bk7258_boottrace.h"
20: #include "bk7258_smp.h"
21: 
22: #define BK7258_IPI_SCHED        (1u << 0)
23: #define BK7258_IPI_CALL         (1u << 1)
24: #define BK7258_IPI_RETRY_LIMIT  1024
25: 
26: #define BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_NOTIFY (BK7258_MBOX_RAW_KICK + 1u)
27: #define BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_PING   (BK7258_MBOX_RAW_KICK + 2u)
28: #define BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_ACK    (BK7258_MBOX_RAW_KICK + 3u)
29: 
30: #define BK7258_BOOT_SEEN_NOTIFY (1u << 0)
31: #define BK7258_BOOT_SEEN_ACK    (1u << 1)
32: 
33: #define BK7258_IPI_TRACE_ENTRY  0xb1000000u
34: #define BK7258_IPI_TRACE_CLAIM  0xb2000000u
35: #define BK7258_IPI_TRACE_SENT   0xb3000000u
36: #define BK7258_IPI_TRACE_FAIL   0xb4000000u
37: 
38: static atomic_t g_ipi_pending[CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS];
39: static atomic_t g_ipi_kicked[CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS];
40: static uint32_t g_boot_seen;
41: 
42: static void bk7258_smp_trace(uint32_t value)
43: {
44:   if (bk7258_boottrace_primary_stage() == BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_FIRST_IRQ)
45:     {
46:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(4, value);
47:     }
48: }
49: 
50: static int bk7258_smp_boot_send(int cpu, uint32_t command)
51: {
52:   uint32_t data[2] = {command, 0};
53:   int retry;
54: 
55:   UP_DMB();
56:   for (retry = 0; retry < BK7258_IPI_RETRY_LIMIT; retry++)
57:     {
58:       int ret = bk7258_mbox_send((uint8_t)(cpu + 1), data);
59: 
60:       if (ret == OK)
61:         {
62:           return OK;
63:         }
64: 
65:       if (ret != -EAGAIN)
66:         {
67:           return ret;
68:         }
69: 
70:       __asm__ volatile("nop");
71:     }
72: 
73:   return -ETIMEDOUT;
74: }
75: 
76: static int bk7258_smp_kick(int cpu, uint32_t pending)
77: {
78:   uint32_t data[2] = {BK7258_MBOX_RAW_KICK, 0};
79:   int expected = 0;
80:   int retry;
81: 
82:   if ((unsigned int)cpu >= CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS || cpu == this_cpu())
83:     {
84:       return -EINVAL;
85:     }
86: 
87:   bk7258_smp_trace(BK7258_IPI_TRACE_ENTRY | (pending & 0xffu));
88:   atomic_or_release(&g_ipi_pending[cpu], pending);
89:   if (!atomic_cmpxchg_acquire(&g_ipi_kicked[cpu], &expected, 1))
90:     {
91:       bk7258_smp_trace(BK7258_IPI_TRACE_CLAIM | 0x100u);
92:       return OK;
93:     }
94: 
95:   bk7258_smp_trace(BK7258_IPI_TRACE_CLAIM | (cpu & 0xffu));
96:   UP_DMB();
97:   for (retry = 0; retry < BK7258_IPI_RETRY_LIMIT; retry++)
98:     {
99:       int ret = bk7258_mbox_send((uint8_t)(cpu + 1), data);
100: 
101:       if (ret == OK)
102:         {
103:           bk7258_smp_trace(BK7258_IPI_TRACE_SENT | (retry & 0xffffu));
104:           return OK;
105:         }
106: 
107:       if (ret != -EAGAIN)
108:         {
109:           atomic_set_release(&g_ipi_kicked[cpu], 0);
110:           bk7258_smp_trace(BK7258_IPI_TRACE_FAIL |
111:                            ((uint32_t)(-ret) & 0xffffu));
112:           return ret;
113:         }
114: 
115:       __asm__ volatile("nop");
116:     }
117: 
118:   atomic_set_release(&g_ipi_kicked[cpu], 0);
119:   bk7258_smp_trace(BK7258_IPI_TRACE_FAIL | 0xffffu);
120:   return -ETIMEDOUT;
121: }
122: 
123: void bk7258_smp_ipi_receive(int irq, void *context, uint32_t command)
124: {
125:   int cpu = this_cpu();
126: 
127:   if (command == BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_NOTIFY)
128:     {
129:       if (cpu == 0)
130:         {
131:           g_boot_seen |= BK7258_BOOT_SEEN_NOTIFY;
132:         }
133: 
134:       return;
135:     }
136: 
137:   if (command == BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_PING)
138:     {
139:       if (cpu == 1 &&
140:           bk7258_smp_boot_send(0, BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_ACK) < 0)
141:         {
142:           PANIC();
143:         }
144: 
145:       bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_ACK);
146:       return;
147:     }
148: 
149:   if (command == BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_ACK)
150:     {
151:       if (cpu == 0)
152:         {
153:           g_boot_seen |= BK7258_BOOT_SEEN_ACK;
154:         }
155: 
156:       return;
157:     }
158: 
159:   if (command != BK7258_MBOX_RAW_KICK)
160:     {
161:       return;
162:     }
163: 
164:   for (;;)
165:     {
166:       uint32_t pending = atomic_xchg_acquire(&g_ipi_pending[cpu], 0);
167: 
168:       if ((pending & BK7258_IPI_CALL) != 0)
169:         {
170:           nxsched_smp_call_handler(irq, context, NULL);
171:         }
172: 
173:       if ((pending & BK7258_IPI_SCHED) != 0)
174:         {
175:           nxsched_process_delivered(cpu);
176:         }
177: 
178:       atomic_set_release(&g_ipi_kicked[cpu], 0);
179:       UP_DMB();
180:       if (atomic_read_acquire(&g_ipi_pending[cpu]) == 0)
181:         {
182:           break;
183:         }
184: 
185:       atomic_set_release(&g_ipi_kicked[cpu], 1);
186:     }
187: }
188: 
189: int up_send_smp_sched(int cpu)
190: {
191:   int ret = bk7258_smp_kick(cpu, BK7258_IPI_SCHED);
192: 
193:   if (ret < 0)
194:     {
195:       return ret;
196:     }
197: 
198:   return ret;
199: }
200: 
201: void bk7258_smp_retry_pending(void)
202: {
203:   if (this_cpu() == 0 && atomic_read_acquire(&g_ipi_pending[1]) != 0 &&
204:       atomic_read_acquire(&g_ipi_kicked[1]) == 0)
205:     {
206:       (void)bk7258_smp_kick(1, 0);
207:     }
208: }
209: 
210: void up_send_smp_call(cpu_set_t cpuset)
211: {
212:   int cpu;
213: 
214:   for (; cpuset != 0; cpuset &= ~(1u << cpu))
215:     {
216:       cpu = ffs((int)cpuset) - 1;
217:       if (cpu != this_cpu() && bk7258_smp_kick(cpu, BK7258_IPI_CALL) < 0)
218:         {
219:           /* The pending call bit remains set for a later coalesced kick. */
220:         }
221:     }
222: }
223: 
224: void bk7258_smp_prepare_boot(void)
225: {
226:   int cpu;
227: 
228:   for (cpu = 0; cpu < CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS; cpu++)
229:     {
230:       atomic_set(&g_ipi_pending[cpu], 0);
231:       atomic_set(&g_ipi_kicked[cpu], 0);
232:     }
233: 
234:   g_boot_seen = 0;
235:   UP_DMB();
236: }
237: 
238: void bk7258_smp_boot_notify(void)
239: {
240:   if (bk7258_smp_boot_send(0, BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_NOTIFY) < 0)
241:     {
242:       PANIC();
243:     }
244: }
245: 
246: bool bk7258_smp_boot_notified(void)
247: {
248:   return (g_boot_seen & BK7258_BOOT_SEEN_NOTIFY) != 0;
249: }
250: 
251: bool bk7258_smp_boot_test_complete(void)
252: {
253:   return g_boot_seen == (BK7258_BOOT_SEEN_NOTIFY |
254:                          BK7258_BOOT_SEEN_ACK);
255: }
256: 
257: int bk7258_smp_boot_ping(int cpu)
258: {
259:   return bk7258_smp_boot_send(cpu, BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_PING);
260: }

2:  * BK7258 MBOX0 v2 physical transport.
3:  ****************************************************************************/
4: 
5: #include <nuttx/config.h>
6: 
7: #include <errno.h>
8: #include <stdbool.h>
9: #include <stdint.h>
10: #include <string.h>
11: 
12: #include <nuttx/arch.h>
13: #include <nuttx/irq.h>
14: 
15: #include "arm_internal.h"
16: #include "hardware/bk7258_mbox.h"
17: #include "hardware/bk7258_sysctrl.h"
18: #include "bk7258_boottrace.h"
19: #include "irq.h"
20: 
21: #define MBOX_RX_DESC_COUNT      (2u * 3u + 1u)
22: #define MBOX_IRQ_DRAIN_BUDGET   8u
23: 
24: struct mbox_rx_descriptor
25: {
26:   struct bk7258_mb_wire_message message;
27:   uint32_t order;
28:   bool used;
29: };
30: 
31: static bk7258_mbox_callback_t g_callback;
32: static struct mbox_rx_descriptor g_rx_desc[MBOX_RX_DESC_COUNT];
33: static uint32_t g_rx_order;
34: static uint32_t g_processing_order;
35: static bool g_mbox_ready;
36: static bool g_mbox_smp_ready;
37: static struct bk7258_mbox_stats g_stats;
38: 
39: static void mbox_trace_errors(void)
40: {
41:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(4,
42:     (g_stats.bad_source & 0xffu) |
43:     ((g_stats.bad_length & 0xffu) << 8) |
44:     ((g_stats.bad_address & 0xffu) << 16) |
45:     ((g_stats.descriptor_full & 0xffu) << 24));
46: }
47: 
48: _Static_assert(MBOX_RX_DESC_COUNT > 2u * 3u,
49:                "RX descriptors must hold a deferred command and two FIFOs");
50: 
51: uint32_t bk7258_mbox_rx_status(void)
52: {
53:   return getreg32(up_cpu_index() == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_STATUS :
54:                                        BK7258_MBOX_CH2_STATUS);
55: }
56: 
57: static void mbox_clear_errors(int cpu)
58: {
59:   uintptr_t cfg = cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_CFG : BK7258_MBOX_CH2_CFG;
60:   uint32_t config = getreg32(cfg);
61:   uint32_t errors = config & BK7258_MBOX_CFG_ERROR_STATUS;
62: 
63:   if (cpu == 0 && (errors & BK7258_MBOX_CFG_WRERR_STATUS) != 0)
64:     {
65:       g_stats.write_error++;
66:     }
67: 
68:   if (cpu == 0 && (errors & BK7258_MBOX_CFG_RDERR_STATUS) != 0)
69:     {
70:       g_stats.read_error++;
71:     }
72: 
73:   if (cpu == 0 && (errors & BK7258_MBOX_CFG_WRFULL_STATUS) != 0)
74:     {
75:       g_stats.write_full++;
76:     }
77: 
78:   if (errors != 0)
79:     {
80:       putreg32((config & BK7258_MBOX_CFG_RW_MASK) | errors, cfg);
81:     }
82: }

84: static bool mbox_valid_envelope(uint8_t source, uint32_t address,
85:                                 uint32_t length)
86: {
87:   if (source != 0)
88:     {
89:       g_stats.bad_source++;
90:       mbox_trace_errors();
91:       return false;
92:     }
93: 
94:   if (length != BK7258_MB_MESSAGE_SIZE)
95:     {
96:       g_stats.bad_length++;
97:       mbox_trace_errors();
98:       return false;
99:     }
100: 
101:   if ((address & 3u) != 0 || address < BK7258_CP_RAM_START ||
102:       address > BK7258_CP_RAM_END - BK7258_MB_MESSAGE_SIZE)
103:     {
104:       g_stats.bad_address++;
105:       mbox_trace_errors();
106:       return false;
107:     }
108: 
109:   return true;
110: }

112: int bk7258_mbox_send(uint8_t destination, const uint32_t data[2])
113: {
114:   uintptr_t status;
115:   int cpu = up_cpu_index();
116: 
117:   if (!g_mbox_ready || destination > 2 || data == NULL)
118:     {
119:       return -EINVAL;
120:     }
121: 
122: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
123:   if (cpu == 1 && (destination != 1 || data[1] != 0))
124:     {
125:       return -EPERM;
126:     }
127: #endif
128: 
129:   /* CPU1 transmits through channel 1.  Full is reported by the target's
130:    * receive FIFO status register.
131:    */
132: 
133:   status = destination == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH0_STATUS :
134:             destination == 1 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_STATUS :
135:                                BK7258_MBOX_CH2_STATUS;
136:   if ((getreg32(status) & 1u) != 0)
137:     {
138:       return -EAGAIN;
139:     }
140: 
141:   putreg32(data[0], cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_TDATA0 :
142:                                BK7258_MBOX_CH2_TDATA0);
143:   putreg32(data[1], cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_TDATA1 :
144:                                BK7258_MBOX_CH2_TDATA1);
145:   putreg32(destination, cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_TID :
146:                                   BK7258_MBOX_CH2_TID);
147:   return OK;
148: }
149: 
150: static struct mbox_rx_descriptor *mbox_alloc_desc(void)
151: {
152:   unsigned int i;
153: 
154:   for (i = 0; i < MBOX_RX_DESC_COUNT; i++)
155:     {
156:       if (!g_rx_desc[i].used)
157:         {
158:           return &g_rx_desc[i];
159:         }
160:     }
161: 
162:   return NULL;
163: }
164: 
165: static bool mbox_priority_message(
166:   const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *message)
167: {
168:   uint8_t control = bk7258_mb_header_ctrl(message);
169: 
170:   return (control & (BK7258_MB_CTRL_ACK_BOX | BK7258_MB_CTRL_RESET)) != 0;
171: }
172: 
173: static struct mbox_rx_descriptor *mbox_oldest_desc(bool priority)
174: {
175:   struct mbox_rx_descriptor *oldest = NULL;
176:   unsigned int i;
177: 
178:   for (i = 0; i < MBOX_RX_DESC_COUNT; i++)
179:     {
180:       struct mbox_rx_descriptor *desc = &g_rx_desc[i];
181: 
182:       if (!desc->used || mbox_priority_message(&desc->message) != priority)
183:         {
184:           continue;
185:         }
186: 
187:       if (oldest == NULL || (int32_t)(desc->order - oldest->order) < 0)
188:         {
189:           oldest = desc;
190:         }
191:     }
192: 
193:   return oldest;
194: }

196: static void mbox_process_desc(void)
197: {
198:   struct mbox_rx_descriptor *desc;
199:   int ret;
200: 
201:   /* ACK and RESET never need ACK slots.  Process them ahead of a deferred
202:    * ordinary command, then retry ordinary commands in original FIFO order.
203:    */
204: 
205:   while ((desc = mbox_oldest_desc(true)) != NULL)
206:     {
207:       g_processing_order = desc->order;
208:       ret = g_callback == NULL ? -ENOSYS : g_callback(&desc->message);
209:       g_processing_order = 0;
210:       if (ret == -EAGAIN)
211:         {
212:           g_stats.descriptor_deferred++;
213:           break;
214:         }
215: 
216:       desc->used = false;
217:     }
218: 
219:   while ((desc = mbox_oldest_desc(false)) != NULL)
220:     {
221:       g_processing_order = desc->order;
222:       ret = g_callback == NULL ? -ENOSYS : g_callback(&desc->message);
223:       g_processing_order = 0;
224:       if (ret == -EAGAIN)
225:         {
226:           break;
227:         }
228: 
229:       desc->used = false;
230:     }
231: }
232: 
233: static int bk7258_mbox_irq(int irq, void *context, void *arg)
234: {
235:   uintptr_t rdata0;
236:   uintptr_t rdata1;
237:   uintptr_t sidreg;
238:   int cpu = up_cpu_index();
239:   unsigned int budget = MBOX_IRQ_DRAIN_BUDGET;
240: 
241:   (void)irq;
242:   (void)context;
243:   (void)arg;
244: 
245:   mbox_clear_errors(cpu);
246:   if (cpu == 1 && bk7258_boottrace_secondary_stage() >=
247:                   BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_ACK &&
248:                   bk7258_boottrace_secondary_stage() <
249:                   BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX_ENTER)
250:     {
251:       bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX_ENTER);
252:     }
253:   sidreg = cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_SID : BK7258_MBOX_CH2_SID;
254:   rdata0 = cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_RDATA0 : BK7258_MBOX_CH2_RDATA0;
255:   rdata1 = cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_RDATA1 : BK7258_MBOX_CH2_RDATA1;
256: 
257:   while ((bk7258_mbox_rx_status() & 2u) == 0 && budget-- != 0)
258:     {
259:       struct mbox_rx_descriptor *desc;
260:       uint32_t address;
261:       uint32_t length;
262:       uint8_t source;
263: 
264:       if (cpu == 0)
265:         {
266:           mbox_process_desc();
267:         }
268: 
269:       desc = cpu == 0 ? mbox_alloc_desc() : NULL;
270:       if (cpu == 0 && desc == NULL)
271:         {
272:           g_stats.descriptor_full++;
273:           mbox_trace_errors();
274:           break;
275:         }
276: 
277:       source = getreg32(sidreg) & 0x0fu;
278:       address = getreg32(rdata0);
279:       length = getreg32(rdata1);
280: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
281:       if (length == 0)
282:         {
283:           if (source == (uint8_t)(2 - cpu))
284:             {
285:               if (cpu == 1 && address == BK7258_MBOX_RAW_KICK)
286:                 {
287:                   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX_RAW);
288:                 }
289: 
290:               bk7258_smp_ipi_receive(irq, context, address);
291:             }
292:           else
293:             {
294:               if (cpu == 0)
295:                 {
296:                   g_stats.bad_source++;
297:                   mbox_trace_errors();
298:                 }
299:             }
300: 
301:           continue;
302:         }
303: #endif
304: 
305:       if (cpu != 0)
306:         {
307:           continue;
308:         }
309: 
310:       if (!mbox_valid_envelope(source, address, length))
311:         {
312:           continue;
313:         }
314: 
315:       __asm__ volatile("dmb sy" ::: "memory");
316:       memcpy(&desc->message, (const void *)(uintptr_t)address,
317:              sizeof(desc->message));
318:       desc->order = ++g_rx_order;
319:       desc->used = true;
320:       g_stats.rx_messages++;
321:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(0, desc->message.header);
322:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(1, address);
323:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(2, g_stats.rx_messages);
324:       mbox_process_desc();
325:     }
326: 
327:   if (cpu == 0)
328:     {
329:       mbox_process_desc();
330:     }
331: 
332:   if (cpu == 1 && bk7258_boottrace_secondary_stage() ==
333:                   BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX_RAW)
334:     {
335:       bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX_EXIT);
336:     }
337: 
338:   return OK;
339: }
340: 
341: void bk7258_mbox_set_callback(bk7258_mbox_callback_t callback)
342: {
343:   g_callback = callback;
344: }

346: void bk7258_mbox_kick_rx(void)
347: {
348:   irqstate_t flags = up_irq_save();

354: void bk7258_mbox_discard_deferred(void)

356:   unsigned int i;
357: 
358:   for (i = 0; i < MBOX_RX_DESC_COUNT; i++)
359:     {
360:       if (g_rx_desc[i].used && g_processing_order != 0 &&
361:           (int32_t)(g_rx_desc[i].order - g_processing_order) < 0 &&
362:           !mbox_priority_message(&g_rx_desc[i].message))

383: int bk7258_mbox_init(void)

385:   int ret;

389:       return OK;
390:     }

392:   memset(g_rx_desc, 0, sizeof(g_rx_desc));

397:   /* CPU1 owns channel 1 and FIFO entries 2..4.  Install the callback and

408:             BK7258_MBOX_CFG_RDERR_EN | BK7258_MBOX_CFG_WRFULL_EN,
409:             BK7258_MBOX_CH2_CFG);

30: static inline void bk7258_route_irq(int extirq, bool enable)
31: {
32:   uintptr_t regaddr;
33:   uint32_t bit;
34:   int cpu = up_cpu_index();

36: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP

40:     }

43:   if (extirq < 32)
44:     {
45:       regaddr = cpu == 0 ? BK7258_CPU1_IRQ_EN0 : BK7258_CPU2_IRQ_EN0;
46:       bit = 1u << extirq;
47:     }
48:   else
49:     {
50:       regaddr = cpu == 0 ? BK7258_CPU1_IRQ_EN1 : BK7258_CPU2_IRQ_EN1;
51:       bit = 1u << (extirq - 32);
52:     }
53: 
54:   if (enable)
55:     {
56:       modifyreg32(regaddr, 0, bit);
57:     }
58:   else
59:     {
60:       modifyreg32(regaddr, bit, 0);

71:   for (i = 0; i < BK7258_EXTIRQ_COUNT; i += 32)
72:     {
73:       putreg32(0xffffffffu, NVIC_IRQ_CLEAR(i));
74:       putreg32(0xffffffffu, NVIC_IRQ_CLRPEND(i));

77:   putreg32(0, BK7258_CPU2_IRQ_EN0);
78:   putreg32(0, BK7258_CPU2_IRQ_EN1);

81:   putreg32(DEFPRIORITY32, NVIC_SYSH4_7_PRIORITY);
82:   putreg32(DEFPRIORITY32, NVIC_SYSH8_11_PRIORITY);
83:   putreg32(DEFPRIORITY32, NVIC_SYSH12_15_PRIORITY);

86:   regaddr = NVIC_IRQ0_3_PRIORITY;

100: static int bk7258_irqinfo(int irq, uintptr_t *regaddr, uint32_t *bit,
101:                           uintptr_t offset)
102: {
103:   int extirq;
104: 
105:   DEBUGASSERT(irq >= BK7258_IRQ_NMI && irq < NR_IRQS);
106: 
107:   if (irq >= BK7258_IRQ_FIRST)
108:     {
109:       extirq = irq - BK7258_IRQ_FIRST;
110:       *regaddr = NVIC_IRQ_ENABLE(extirq) + offset;
111:       *bit = 1u << (extirq & 31);
112:       return OK;
113:     }
114: 
115:   *regaddr = NVIC_SYSHCON;
116:   switch (irq)
117:     {
118:       case BK7258_IRQ_MEMFAULT:
119:         *bit = NVIC_SYSHCON_MEMFAULTENA;
120:         break;
121:       case BK7258_IRQ_BUSFAULT:
122:         *bit = NVIC_SYSHCON_BUSFAULTENA;
123:         break;
124:       case BK7258_IRQ_USAGEFAULT:
125:         *bit = NVIC_SYSHCON_USGFAULTENA;
126:         break;
127:       case BK7258_IRQ_SECUREFAULT:
128:         *bit = NVIC_SYSHCON_SECUREFAULTENA;
129:         break;
130:       case BK7258_IRQ_SYSTICK:
131:         *regaddr = NVIC_SYSTICK_CTRL;
132:         *bit = NVIC_SYSTICK_CTRL_ENABLE;
133:         break;
134:       default:
135:         return ERROR;
136:     }
137: 
138:   return OK;
139: }

141: static inline void bk7258_prioritize_svcall(int priority)
142: {
143:   uint32_t regval = getreg32(NVIC_SYSH8_11_PRIORITY);
144:   regval &= ~NVIC_SYSH_PRIORITY_PR11_MASK;
145:   regval |= priority << NVIC_SYSH_PRIORITY_PR11_SHIFT;
146:   putreg32(regval, NVIC_SYSH8_11_PRIORITY);
147: }

160:   putreg32(0, BK7258_CPU1_IRQ_EN0);

163:   putreg32(DEFPRIORITY32, NVIC_SYSH4_7_PRIORITY);

165:   putreg32(DEFPRIORITY32, NVIC_SYSH12_15_PRIORITY);

175:   irq_attach(BK7258_IRQ_SVCALL, arm_svcall, NULL);
176:   irq_attach(BK7258_IRQ_HARDFAULT, arm_hardfault, NULL);
177:   irq_attach(BK7258_IRQ_MEMFAULT, arm_memfault, NULL);
178:   irq_attach(BK7258_IRQ_BUSFAULT, arm_busfault, NULL);

181:   arm_enable_dbgmonitor();
182:   irq_attach(BK7258_IRQ_DBGMONITOR, arm_dbgmonitor, NULL);

184:   bk7258_prioritize_svcall(NVIC_SYSH_SVCALL_PRIORITY);
185:   up_enable_irq(BK7258_IRQ_MEMFAULT);
186:   up_enable_irq(BK7258_IRQ_BUSFAULT);

12: 
13: extern void __start(void);
14: extern void exception_common(void);
15: extern void exception_direct(void);
16: extern uint8_t __idle_stack_top[];
17: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
18: extern void bk7258_secondary_start(void);
19: extern uint8_t __secondary_boot_stack_top[];
20: #endif
21: 
22: typedef void (*vector_t)(void);
23: 
24: /* CPU0 starts CPU1 at the AP image origin, so this table must remain at raw
25:  * image offset zero. The BK legacy words at 0x100 make it unsuitable as the
26:  * runtime vector table.
27:  */
28: 
29: const vector_t g_bk7258_boot_vectors[NR_IRQS]
30:   __attribute__((used, section(".bk_boot_vectors"), aligned(512))) =
31: {
32:   [0]       = (vector_t)__idle_stack_top,
33:   [1]       = __start,
34:   [2 ... 14] = exception_common,
35:   [15 ... 63] = exception_direct,
36:   [64]      = (vector_t)0x32374b42u,
37:   [65]      = (vector_t)0x00003633u,
38:   [66 ... (NR_IRQS - 1)] = exception_direct,
39: };
40: 
41: /* NuttX exceptions enter through the common ARMv8-M assembly dispatchers.
42:  * This complete table is copied to AP SRAM before interrupts are enabled.
43:  */

96: /* Common exception handling logic.  On entry here, the return stack is on either
97:  * the PSP or the MSP and looks like the following:
98:  *
99:  *      REG_XPSR
100:  *      REG_R15
101:  *      REG_R14
102:  *      REG_R12
103:  *      REG_R3
104:  *      REG_R2
105:  *      REG_R1
106:  * MSP->REG_R0
107:  *
108:  * And
109:  *      IPSR contains the IRQ number
110:  *      R14 Contains the EXC_RETURN value
111:  *      We are in handler mode and the current SP is the MSP
112:  *
113:  * If CONFIG_ARCH_FPU is defined, the volatile FP registers and FPSCR are on the
114:  * return stack immediately above REG_XPSR.
115:  */
116: 
117: 	.text
118: 	.align 2
119: 	.section    .text.exception_common, "ax"
120: #ifdef __ghs__
121: 	.type	exception_common, $function
122: #else
123: 	.thumb_func
124: 	.syntax	unified
125: 	.type	exception_common, function
126: #endif
127: exception_common:
128: 	.cfi_sections	.debug_frame
129: 	.cfi_startproc
130: 	mrs		r12, control				/* R12=control */
131: 
132: #ifdef CONFIG_ARMV8M_STACKCHECK_HARDWARE
133: 	mov		r3, #0x0
134: #endif
135: 	/* Complete the context save */
136: 
137: 	/* The EXC_RETURN value tells us whether the context is on the MSP or PSP */
138: 
139: 	mov		r0, r14					/* Copy EXC_RETURN */
140: 	lsls		r0, #(31 - EXC_RETURN_PROCESS_BITNO)	/* Move to bit 31 */
141: 	bpl		1f					/* Test bit 31 */
142: 	mrs		r1, psp					/* R1=The process stack pointer (PSP) */
143: #ifdef CONFIG_ARMV8M_STACKCHECK_HARDWARE
144: 	mrs		r0, psplim
145: 	msr		psplim, r3
146: #endif

148: 1:
149: 	mrs		r1, msp					/* R1=The main stack pointer (MSP) */
150: 	mov		r0, r1					/* Keep r1 not changed for push */
151: 	subs		r0, #SW_XCPT_SIZE			/* Reserve MSP for SW_XCPT_SIZE */
152: 	msr		msp, r0					/* Reserved stack space */
153: #ifdef CONFIG_ARMV8M_STACKCHECK_HARDWARE
154: 	mrs		r0, msplim
155: 	msr		msplim, r3
156: #endif
157: 	isb		sy
158: 2:
159: 	mov		r2, r1					/* R2=Copy of the main/process stack pointer */
160: 	adds		r2, #HW_XCPT_SIZE			/* R2=MSP/PSP before the interrupt was taken */
161: 								/* (ignoring the xPSR[9] alignment bit) */
162: #ifdef CONFIG_ARMV8M_STACKCHECK_HARDWARE
163: 	stmdb		r1!, {r0, r3}
164: #endif
165: 
166: #ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_ARMV6M
167: 	mrs		r3, primask				/* R3=Current PRIMASK setting */
168: #else
169: 	mrs		r3, basepri				/* R3=Current BASEPRI setting */
170: #endif /* CONFIG_ARCH_ARMV6M */
171: 
172: #ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_FPU
173: 
174: 	/* Save the non-volatile FP registers here.
175: 	 *
176: 	 * This routine is the only point where we can save these registers; either before
177: 	 * or after calling arm_doirq.  The compiler is free to use them at any time as long
178: 	 * as they are restored before returning, so we can't assume that we can get at the
179: 	 * true values of these registers in any routine called from here.
180: 	 *
181: 	 * REVISIT: we could do all this saving lazily on the context switch side if we knew
182: 	 * where to put the registers.
183: 	 */
184: 
185: 	/* Switched-out task including volatile FP registers ? */
186: 
187: 	tst		r14, #EXC_RETURN_STD_CONTEXT
188: 	ite		eq
189: 	vstmdbeq	r1!, {s16-s31}			/* Save the non-volatile FP context */
190: 	subne		r1, #(4*SW_FPU_REGS)
191: 
192: 	/* the FPSCR[18:16] LTPSIZE field must be set to 0b100 for
193: 	 * "Tail predication not applied" as it's reset value.
194: 	 */
195: 
196: 	mov		r0, #ARM_FPSCR_LTPSIZE_NONE

198: #endif
199: 
200: #ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_ARMV6M
201: 	subs		r1, #(4*SW_INT_REGS)		/* Move cursor to base, for save low regs first */
202: 	mov		r0, r1				/* Copy the context array pointer */
203: 	stmia		r0!, {r2-r7}			/* Save the SP, PRIMASK, and R4-R7 in the context array */

207: 	mov		r2, r8				/* Copy high registers to low */
208: 	mov		r3, r9
209: 	mov		r4, r10
210: 	mov		r5, r11
211: 	mrs		r6, control			/* R6=control */
212: 	mov		r7, r14
213: 	stmia		r0!, {r2-r7}			/* Save the high registers r8-r11 control and r14 */
214: #else
215: 	stmdb		r1!, {r2-r12,r14}		/* Save the remaining registers plus the SP/PRIMASK values */
216: #endif /* CONFIG_ARCH_ARMV6M */

218: 	/* There are two arguments to arm_doirq:
219: 	 *
220: 	 *   R0 = The IRQ number
221: 	 *   R1 = The top of the stack points to the saved state
222: 	 */
223: 
224: 	mrs		r0, ipsr			/* R0=exception number */
225: 
226: #if CONFIG_ARCH_INTERRUPTSTACK < 7
227: 	/* If CONFIG_ARCH_INTERRUPTSTACK is not defined, we will reuse the
228: 	 * interrupted thread's stack.  That may mean using either MSP or PSP

246: #ifndef CONFIG_DISABLE_SIGNALS

248: 	subs		r2, #XCPTCONTEXT_SIZE			/* Reserve signal context */

273: 	mov		r9, r3
274: 	mov		r10, r4
275: 	mov		r11, r5
276: 	msr		control, r6
277: 	mov		r14, r7			/* EXEC_RETURN */
278: 
279: 	/* Recover SP (R2), PRIMASK (R3), and R4-R7. Determine the value of
280: 	 * the stack pointer as it was on entry to the exception handler.
281: 	 */
282: 
283: 	movs		r1, #(4*REG_R8)		/* Already restored offset */
284: 	ldmia		r0!, {r2-r7}		/* Recover R4-R7 + 2 temp values */
285: 	adds		r0, r0, r1		/* Fix already restored R8-R11 and R14 popped address */
286: #else
287: 	ldmia		r0!, {r2-r12,r14}	/* Recover R4-R12, r14 + 2 temp values */
288: #endif /* CONFIG_ARCH_ARMV6M */
289: #ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_FPU
290: 	/* Switched-in task including volatile FP registers ? */
291: 
292: 	tst		r14, #EXC_RETURN_STD_CONTEXT
293: 	ite		eq
294: 	vldmiaeq	r0!, {s16-s31}		/* Recover S16-S31 */
295: 	addne		r0, #(4*SW_FPU_REGS)
296: #endif
297: 
298: #ifdef CONFIG_ARMV8M_STACKCHECK_HARDWARE
299: 	ldmia		r0!, {r1}		/* Get psplim/msplim */
300: 	add		r0, r0, #4
301: #endif
302: 
303: 	/* The EXC_RETURN value tells us whether we are returning on the MSP or PSP
304: 	 */
305: 
306: 	mov		r2, r14					/* Copy EXC_RETURN */
307: 	lsls		r2, #(31 - EXC_RETURN_PROCESS_BITNO)	/* Move to bit 31 */
308: 	bmi		4f					/* Test bit 31 */
309: 	msr		msp, r0					/* R1=The main stack pointer */
310: #ifdef CONFIG_ARMV8M_STACKCHECK_HARDWARE
311: 	msr		msplim, r1
312: #endif
313: 	b		5f
314: 4:
315: 	msr		psp, r0					/* R1=The process stack pointer */
316: #ifdef CONFIG_ARMV8M_STACKCHECK_HARDWARE
317: 	msr		psplim, r1
318: #endif
319: 5:
320: 	isb		sy
321: 
322: 	/* Restore the interrupt state */
323: 
324: #ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_ARMV6M
325: 	msr		primask, r3				/* Restore interrupts priority masking*/
326: #else
327: 	msr		basepri, r3				/* Restore interrupts priority masking */
328: #endif /* CONFIG_ARCH_ARMV6M */
329: 
330: 	msr		control, r12				/* Restore control */
331: 	isb		sy
332: 
333: 	/* Always return with R14 containing the special value that will: (1)
334: 	 * return to thread mode, and (2) select the correct stack.
335: 	 */
336: 
337: 	bx		r14					/* And return */
338: 	.cfi_endproc
339: 	.size	exception_common, .-exception_common
340:

103: #endif

105:       up_irq_save();
106:     }

118:        * running task is closed down gracefully (data caches dump,

144:

102:  *   System initialization occurs on that single thread. At the completion
103:  *   of the initialization of the OS, just before beginning normal
104:  *   multitasking, the additional CPUs would be started by calling this
105:  *   function.

107:  * Input Parameters:
108:  *   None

111:  *   Zero on success; a negated errno value on failure.

114:  *   Runs before the full initialization sequence has completed.  Runs after
115:  *   all OS facilities are set up, but before multi-tasking has been started.
116:  *
117:  ****************************************************************************/

119: int nx_smp_start(void)
120: {
121:   int ret;
122:   int cpu;
123: 
124:   /* Flush dcache before start other CPUs. */
125:

77:  * Name: fifo_drain
78:  *
79:  * Description:
80:  *   Drain all data in the inter-processor FIFO
81:  ****************************************************************************/
82: 
83: static void fifo_drain(void)
84: {
85:   putreg32(0, RP2040_SIO_FIFO_ST);
86: 
87:   while (getreg32(RP2040_SIO_FIFO_ST) & RP2040_SIO_FIFO_ST_VLD)
88:     {
89:       getreg32(RP2040_SIO_FIFO_RD);
90:     }
91: 
92:   __asm__ volatile ("sev");
93: }

95: /****************************************************************************
96:  * Name: fifo_comm
97:  *
98:  * Description:
99:  *   Communicate with CPU Core 1 using inter-processor FIFO for boot
100:  *
101:  * Input Parameters:
102:  *   msg - Data to be sent to Core 1
103:  *
104:  * Returned Value:
105:  *   true on success; false on failure.
106:  *
107:  ****************************************************************************/
108: 
109: static int fifo_comm(uint32_t msg)
110: {
111:   uint32_t rcv;
112: 
113:   while (!(getreg32(RP2040_SIO_FIFO_ST) & RP2040_SIO_FIFO_ST_RDY))
114:     ;
115:   putreg32(msg, RP2040_SIO_FIFO_WR);
116:   __asm__ volatile ("sev");
117: 
118:   while (!(getreg32(RP2040_SIO_FIFO_ST) & RP2040_SIO_FIFO_ST_VLD))
119:     __asm__ volatile ("wfe");
120: 
121:   rcv = getreg32(RP2040_SIO_FIFO_RD);
122: 
123:   return msg == rcv;
124: }

174: /****************************************************************************
175:  * Name: up_cpu_start
176:  *
177:  * Description:
178:  *   In an SMP configuration, only one CPU is initially active (CPU 0).
179:  *   System initialization occurs on that single thread. At the completion of
180:  *   the initialization of the OS, just before beginning normal multitasking,
181:  *   the additional CPUs would be started by calling this function.
182:  *
183:  *   Each CPU is provided the entry point to its IDLE task when started.  A
184:  *   TCB for each CPU's IDLE task has been initialized and placed in the
185:  *   CPU's g_assignedtasks[cpu] list.  No stack has been allocated or
186:  *   initialized.
187:  *
188:  *   The OS initialization logic calls this function repeatedly until each
189:  *   CPU has been started, 1 through (CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS-1).
190:  *
191:  * Input Parameters:
192:  *   cpu - The index of the CPU being started.  This will be a numeric
193:  *         value in the range of one to (CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS-1).
194:  *         (CPU 0 is already active)
195:  *
196:  * Returned Value:
197:  *   Zero on success; a negated errno value on failure.
198:  *
199:  ****************************************************************************/
200: 
201: int up_cpu_start(int cpu)
202: {
203:   int i;
204:   struct tcb_s *tcb = current_task(cpu);
205:   uint32_t core1_boot_msg[5];
206: 
207:   DPRINTF("cpu=%d\n", cpu);
208: 
209: #ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_INSTRUMENTATION
210:   /* Notify of the start event */
211: 
212:   sched_note_cpu_start(this_task(), cpu);
213: #endif
214: 
215:   /* Reset Core 1 */
216: 
217:   setbits_reg32(RP2040_PSM_PROC1, RP2040_PSM_FRCE_OFF);
218:   while (!(getreg32(RP2040_PSM_FRCE_OFF) & RP2040_PSM_PROC1))
219:     ;
220:   clrbits_reg32(RP2040_PSM_PROC1, RP2040_PSM_FRCE_OFF);
221: 
222:   spin_lock(&g_core1_boot);
223: 
224:   /* Send initial VTOR, MSP, PC for Core 1 boot */
225: 
226:   core1_boot_msg[0] = 0;
227:   core1_boot_msg[1] = 1;
228:   core1_boot_msg[2] = getreg32(ARMV6M_SYSCON_VECTAB);
229:   core1_boot_msg[3] = (uint32_t)tcb->stack_base_ptr +
230:                                 tcb->adj_stack_size;
231:   core1_boot_msg[4] = (uint32_t)core1_boot;
232: 
233:   do
234:     {
235:       fifo_drain();
236:       for (i = 0; i < 5; i++)
237:         {
238:           if (!fifo_comm(core1_boot_msg[i]))
239:             {
240:               break;
241:             }
242:         }
243:     }
244:   while (i < 5);
245: 
246:   fifo_drain();
247: 
248:   /* Enable inter-processor FIFO interrupt */
249: 
250:   irq_attach(RP2040_SMP_CALL_PROC0, rp2040_smp_call_handler, NULL);
251:   up_enable_irq(RP2040_SMP_CALL_PROC0);
252: 
253:   spin_lock(&g_core1_boot);
254: 
255:   /* CPU Core 1 boot done */
256: 
257:   spin_unlock(&g_core1_boot);
258: 
259:   return 0;
260: }

159:  *         value in the range of one to (CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS-1).
160:  *         (CPU 0 is already active)
161:  *
162:  * Returned Value:
163:  *   Zero on success; a negated errno value on failure.
164:  *
165:  ****************************************************************************/
166: 
167: int up_cpu_start(int cpu)
168: {
169:   int i;
170:   struct tcb_s *tcb = current_task(cpu);
171: 
172:   DPRINTF("cpu=%d\n", cpu);
173: 
174: #ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_INSTRUMENTATION
175:   /* Notify of the start event */
176: 
177:   sched_note_cpu_start(this_task(), cpu);
178: #endif
179: 
180:   /* Reset APP_DSP(cpu) */
181: 
182:   modifyreg32(CXD56_CRG_RESET, 1 << (16 + cpu), 0);
183: 
184:   /* Copy initial stack and reset vector for APP_DSP */
185: 
186:   putreg32((uint32_t)tcb->stack_base_ptr +
187:                      tcb->adj_stack_size, VECTOR_ISTACK);
188:   putreg32((uint32_t)appdsp_boot, VECTOR_RESETV);
189: 
190:   spin_lock(&g_appdsp_boot);
191: 
192:   /* See 3.13.4.16.3 ADSP Startup */
193: 
194:   /* 2. Clock supply */
195: 
196:   modifyreg32(CXD56_CRG_CK_GATE_AHB, 0, 1 << (16 + cpu));
197: 
198:   /* 3. Clock stop */
199: 
200:   modifyreg32(CXD56_CRG_CK_GATE_AHB, 1 << (16 + cpu), 0);
201: 
202:   /* 4. APP_DSP(cpu) start preparation */
203: 
204:   /* Copy APP_DSP0 settings to all 12 tiles for APP_DSP(cpu)
205:    * TODO: need to exclude memory areas for AMP
206:    */
207: 
208:   for (i = 0; i < 12; i++)
209:     {
210:       uint32_t val = getreg32(CXD56_ACNV_P0_DST0 + (4 * i));
211:       putreg32(val, CXD56_ACNV_P0_DST0 + (4 * i) + (cpu * 0x20));
212:     }
213: 
214:   /* 5. Reset release */
215: 
216:   modifyreg32(CXD56_CRG_RESET, 0, 1 << (16 + cpu));
217: 
218:   /* 6. Clock supply */
219: 
220:   modifyreg32(CXD56_CRG_CK_GATE_AHB, 0, 1 << (16 + cpu));
221: 
222:   /* Setup SW_INT for APP_DSP0. The caller is APP_DSP0 and
223:    * it's enough to setup only once. So, here this setup is
224:    * done in case that we boot APP_DSP1 (cpu=1).
225:    */
226: 
227:   if (1 == cpu)
228:     {
229:       /* Clear SW_INT for this APP_DSP0 */
230: 
231:       putreg32(0, CXD56_CPU_P2_INT);
232: 
233:       /* Setup SW_INT for this APP_DSP0 */
234: 
235:       irq_attach(CXD56_IRQ_SMP_CALL, cxd56_smp_call_handler, NULL);
236:       up_enable_irq(CXD56_IRQ_SMP_CALL);
237:     }
238: 
239:   spin_lock(&g_appdsp_boot);
240: 
241:   /* APP_DSP(cpu) boot done */
242: 
243:   spin_unlock(&g_appdsp_boot);
244: 
245:   return 0;

130: /****************************************************************************
131:  * Name: up_cpu_start
132:  *
133:  * Description:
134:  *   In an SMP configuration, only one CPU is initially active (CPU 0).
135:  *   System initialization occurs on that single thread. At the completion of
136:  *   the initialization of the OS, just before beginning normal multitasking,
137:  *   the additional CPUs would be started by calling this function.
138:  *
139:  *   Each CPU is provided the entry point to its IDLE task when started.  A
140:  *   TCB for each CPU's IDLE task has been initialized and placed in the
141:  *   CPU's g_assignedtasks[cpu] list.  No stack has been allocated or
142:  *   initialized.
143:  *
144:  *   The OS initialization logic calls this function repeatedly until each
145:  *   CPU has been started, 1 through (CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS-1).
146:  *
147:  * Input Parameters:
148:  *   cpu - The index of the CPU being started.  This will be a numeric
149:  *         value in the range of one to (CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS-1).
150:  *         (CPU 0 is already active)
151:  *
152:  * Returned Value:
153:  *   Zero on success; a negated errno value on failure.
154:  *
155:  ****************************************************************************/
156: 
157: int up_cpu_start(int cpu)
158: {
159:   struct tcb_s *tcb = current_task(cpu);
160:   uint32_t backup[2];
161: 
162:   DPRINTF("cpu=%d\n", cpu);
163: 
164:   if (cpu != 1)
165:     {
166:       return -1;
167:     }
168: 
169:   /* create initial vectors for CPU1 */
170: 
171:   putreg32(0x1, REMAP); /* remap enable */
172:   backup[0] = getreg32(CPU1_VECTOR_ISTACK);
173:   backup[1] = getreg32(CPU1_VECTOR_RESETV);
174:   putreg32((uint32_t)tcb->stack_base_ptr +
175:                      tcb->adj_stack_size, CPU1_VECTOR_ISTACK);
176:   putreg32((uint32_t)cpu1_boot, CPU1_VECTOR_RESETV);
177: 
178:   spin_lock(&per_cpu_var_smp(g_cpu_wait, 0));
179: 
180: #ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_INSTRUMENTATION
181:   /* Notify of the start event */
182: 
183:   sched_note_cpu_start(this_task(), cpu);
184: #endif
185: 
186:   /* enable clock core #1 */
187: 
188:   modifyreg32(CORECNT, 0, CORECNT_C1CLKEN);
189: 
190:   /* unreset core #1 */
191: 
192:   modifyreg32(CORECNT, 0, CORECNT_C1RSTN);
193: 
194:   /* IRQ setup CPU1->CPU0 */
195: 
196:   irq_attach(LC823450_IRQ_SMP_CALL_11, lc823450_smp_call_handler, NULL);
197:   up_enable_irq(LC823450_IRQ_SMP_CALL_11);
198: 
199:   spin_lock(&per_cpu_var_smp(g_cpu_wait, 0));
200: 
201:   /* CPU1 boot done */
202: 
203:   /* restore : after CPU1 boot, CPU1 use normal vectors table. */
204: 
205:   putreg32(backup[0], CPU1_VECTOR_ISTACK);
206:   putreg32(backup[1], CPU1_VECTOR_RESETV);
207:   putreg32(0x0, REMAP); /* remap disable */
208: 
209:   spin_unlock(&per_cpu_var_smp(g_cpu_wait, 0));
210: 
211:   return 0;
212: }

34: /* The processor saves an EXC_RETURN value to the LR on exception entry. The
35:  * exception mechanism relies on this value to detect when the processor has
36:  * completed an exception handler.
37:  *
38:  * Bits [31:28] of an EXC_RETURN value are always 1.  When the processor
39:  * loads a value matching this pattern to the PC it detects that the
40:  * operation is a not a normal branch operation and instead, that the
41:  * exception is complete. Therefore, it starts the exception return sequence.
42:  *
43:  * Bits[6:0] of the EXC_RETURN value indicate the required return stack and
44:  * eventual processor mode.
45:  * The remaining bits of the EXC_RETURN value should be set to 1.
46:  */
47: 
48: /* EXC_RETURN_EXC_SECURE: Exception Secure.  The security domain the
49:  * exception was taken to.  If this bit is clear non-secure, else secure.
50:  */
51: 
52: #define EXC_RETURN_EXC_SECURE    (1 << 0)
53: 
54: /* EXC_RETURN_PROCESS_STACK: The exception saved (and will restore) the
55:  * hardware context using the process stack pointer (if not set, the context
56:  * was saved using the main stack pointer)
57:  */
58: 
59: #define EXC_RETURN_PROCESS_BITNO (2)
60: #define EXC_RETURN_PROCESS_STACK (1 << EXC_RETURN_PROCESS_BITNO)
61: 
62: /* EXC_RETURN_THREAD_MODE: The exception will return to thread mode (if not
63:  * set, return stays in handler mode)
64:  */
65: 
66: #define EXC_RETURN_THREAD_BITNO  (3)
67: #define EXC_RETURN_THREAD_MODE   (1 << EXC_RETURN_THREAD_BITNO)
68: 
69: /* EXC_RETURN_STD_CONTEXT: The state saved on the stack does not include the
70:  * volatile FP registers and FPSCR.  If this bit is clear, the state does
71:  * include these registers.
72:  */
73: 
74: #define EXC_RETURN_STD_CONTEXT   (1 << 4)
75: 
76: /* EXC_RETURN_DEF_STACKING: Default callee register stacking (DCRS).
77:  * Indicates whether the default stacking rules apply, or whether the callee
78:  * registers are already on the stack.  The possible values of this bit are:
79:  * 0 - Stacking of the callee saved registers skipped.  1 - Default rules for
80:  * stacking the callee registers followed.
81:  */
82: 
83: #define EXC_RETURN_DEF_STACKING  (1 << 5)
84: 
85: /* EXC_RETURN_SECURE_STACK: Secure or Non-secure stack.  Indicates whether a
86:  * Secure or Non-secure stack is used to restore stack frame on exception
87:  * return.  The possible values of this bit are: 0 -  Non-secure stack used.
88:  * 1 - Secure stack used.
89:  */
90: 
91: #define EXC_RETURN_SECURE_STACK  (1 << 6)
92: 
93: /* EXC_RETURN_BASE: Bits that are always set in an EXC_RETURN value. */
94: 
95: #ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_TRUSTZONE_NONSECURE
96: #  define EXC_RETURN_BASE        (0xffffff80)
97: #else
98: #  define EXC_RETURN_BASE        (0xffffff80 | EXC_RETURN_EXC_SECURE | \
99:                                   EXC_RETURN_SECURE_STACK)
100: #endif
101: 
102: /* EXC_RETURN_HANDLER: Return to handler mode. Exception return gets state
103:  * from the main stack. Execution uses MSP after return.
104:  */
105: 
106: #define EXC_RETURN_HANDLER       (EXC_RETURN_BASE | EXC_RETURN_DEF_STACKING | \
107:                                   EXC_RETURN_STD_CONTEXT)
108: 
109: #ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_FPU
110: #  define EXC_RETURN_FPU         0
111: #else
112: #  define EXC_RETURN_FPU         EXC_RETURN_STD_CONTEXT
113: #endif
114: 
115: #if CONFIG_ARCH_INTERRUPTSTACK > 7
116: #  define EXC_RETURN_STACK       EXC_RETURN_PROCESS_STACK
117: #else
118: #  define EXC_RETURN_STACK       0
119: #endif
120: 
121: /* EXC_RETURN_THREAD: Return to thread mode.
122:  * If EXC_RETURN_STACK is 0, Return to thread mode.
123:  * Execution uses MSP after return.
124:  * If EXC_RETURN_STACK is EXC_RETURN_PROCESS_STACK, Return to
125:  * thread mode. Execution uses PSP after return.
126:  */
127: 
128: #define EXC_RETURN_THREAD        (EXC_RETURN_BASE | EXC_RETURN_FPU | \
129:                                   EXC_RETURN_THREAD_MODE | EXC_RETURN_STACK | \
130:                                   EXC_RETURN_DEF_STACKING)
131: 
132: #ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_FPU
133: #  define EXC_INTEGRITY_SIGNATURE (0xfefa125a)
134: #else
135: #  define EXC_INTEGRITY_SIGNATURE (0xfefa125b)
136: #endif
137: 
138: /* FUNC_RETURN_EXC_SECURE: Exception Secure.  The security domain the
139:  * function was taken to.  If this bit is clear non-secure, else secure.
140:  */
141: 
142: #define FUNC_RETURN_EXC_SECURE   (1 << 0)
143: 
144: /* FUNC_RETURN_BASE: Bits that are always set in a FUNC_RETURN value. */
145: 
146: #define FUNC_RETURN_BASE         (0xfefffffe)

44:  *
45:  * Description:
46:  *   Secure an IRQ
47:  *
48:  ****************************************************************************/
49: 
50: void up_secure_irq(int irq, bool secure)
51: {
52:   uint32_t keymask = 0;
53:   uint32_t keyval = 0;
54:   uint32_t regaddr;
55:   uint32_t regval;
56:   uint32_t regbit;
57: 
58:   switch (irq)
59:     {
60:       case NVIC_IRQ_NMI:
61:       case NVIC_IRQ_HARDFAULT:
62:       case NVIC_IRQ_BUSFAULT:
63:         regaddr = NVIC_AIRCR;
64:         regbit  = NVIC_AIRCR_BFHFNMINS;
65:         keymask = NVIC_AIRCR_VECTKEY_MASK;
66:         keyval  = NVIC_AIRCR_VECTKEY;
67:         break;
68: 
69:       case NVIC_IRQ_DBGMONITOR:
70:         regaddr = NVIC_DAUTHCTRL;
71:         regbit  = NVIC_DAUTHCTRL_SPIDENSEL;
72:         break;
73: 
74:       default:
75:         DEBUGASSERT(irq >= NVIC_IRQ_FIRST && irq < NR_IRQS);
76:         irq    -= NVIC_IRQ_FIRST;
77:         regaddr = NVIC_IRQ_TARGET(irq);
78:         regbit  = 1 << (irq & 0x1f);
79:         break;
80:     }
81: 
82:   regval = getreg32(regaddr);
83:   if (secure)
84:     {
85:       regval &= ~regbit;
86:     }
87:   else
88:     {
89:       regval |= regbit;
90:     }
91: 
92:   regval = (regval & ~keymask) | keyval;
93:   putreg32(regval, regaddr);
94: }
95: 
96: /****************************************************************************
97:  * Name: up_secure_irq_all
98:  *
99:  * Description:
100:  *   Secure all IRQ
101:  *
102:  ****************************************************************************/
103: 
104: void up_secure_irq_all(bool secure)
105: {
106:   int i;
107: 
108:   modreg32((secure ? 0 : NVIC_AIRCR_BFHFNMINS) | NVIC_AIRCR_VECTKEY,
109:            (NVIC_AIRCR_VECTKEY_MASK | NVIC_AIRCR_BFHFNMINS), NVIC_AIRCR);
110: 
111:   modreg32(secure ? NVIC_DEMCR_SDME : 0,
112:            NVIC_DEMCR_SDME, NVIC_DEMCR);
113: 
114:   for (i = 0; i <= NR_IRQS - NVIC_IRQ_FIRST; i += 32)
115:     {
116:       putreg32(secure ? 0x0 : 0xffffffff, NVIC_IRQ_TARGET(i));
117:     }
118: }

32: /****************************************************************************
33:  * Name: arm_fpuconfig
34:  *
35:  * Description:
36:  *   Configure the FPU.  Relative bit settings:
37:  *
38:  *     CPACR:  Enables access to CP10 and CP11
39:  *     CONTROL.FPCA: Determines whether the FP extension is active in the
40:  *       current context:
41:  *     FPCCR.ASPEN:  Enables automatic FP state preservation, then the
42:  *       processor sets this bit to 1 on successful completion of any FP
43:  *       instruction.
44:  *     FPCCR.LSPEN:  Enables lazy context save of FP state. When this is
45:  *       done, the processor reserves space on the stack for the FP state,
46:  *       but does not save that state information to the stack.
47:  *
48:  *  Software must not change the value of the ASPEN bit or LSPEN bit while
49:  *  either:
50:  *
51:  *   - the CPACR permits access to CP10 and CP11, that give access to the FP
52:  *     extension, or
53:  *   - the CONTROL.FPCA bit is set to 1
54:  *
55:  ****************************************************************************/
56: 
57: void arm_fpuconfig(void)
58: {
59:   uint32_t regval;
60: 
61:   /* Set CONTROL.FPCA so that we always get the extended context frame
62:    * with the volatile FP registers stacked above the basic context.
63:    */
64: 
65:   regval = getcontrol();
66:   regval |= CONTROL_FPCA;
67:   setcontrol(regval);
68: 
69:   /* Ensure that FPCCR.LSPEN is disabled, so that we don't have to contend
70:    * with the lazy FP context save behavior.  Clear FPCCR.ASPEN since we
71:    * are going to turn on CONTROL.FPCA for all contexts.
72:    */
73: 
74:   regval = getreg32(NVIC_FPCCR);
75:   regval &= ~(NVIC_FPCCR_ASPEN | NVIC_FPCCR_LSPEN);
76:   putreg32(regval, NVIC_FPCCR);
77: 
78:   /* Enable full access to CP10 and CP11 */
79: 
80:   regval = getreg32(NVIC_CPACR);
81:   regval |= NVIC_CPACR_CP_FULL(10) | NVIC_CPACR_CP_FULL(11);
82:   putreg32(regval, NVIC_CPACR);
83: }

67:  *   exceptions that are performed in bad contexts.
68:  *
69:  ****************************************************************************/

71: int arm_hardfault(int irq, void *context, void *arg)
72: {
73:   uint32_t hfsr = getreg32(NVIC_HFAULTS);
74:   uint32_t cfsr = getreg32(NVIC_CFAULTS);
75: #ifdef CONFIG_DEBUG_SECUREFAULT
76:   uint32_t sfsr = getreg32(SAU_SFSR);
77: #endif /* CONFIG_DEBUG_SECUREFAULT */
78: 
79:   UNUSED(cfsr);
80:   UNUSED(hfsr);
81: 
82: #ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_ARMV6M
83:   uint32_t *regs = (uint32_t *)context;
84:   uint16_t *pc = (uint16_t *)regs[REG_PC] - 1;
85: 
86:   /* Check if the pc lies in known FLASH memory.
87:    * REVISIT:  What if the PC lies in "unknown" external memory?
88:    */
89: 
90: #ifdef CONFIG_BUILD_PROTECTED
91:   /* In the kernel build, SVCalls are expected in either the base, kernel
92:    * FLASH region or in the user FLASH region.
93:    */
94: 
95:   if (((uintptr_t)pc >= (uintptr_t)_stext &&
96:       (uintptr_t)pc <  (uintptr_t)_etext) ||
97:       ((uintptr_t)pc >= (uintptr_t)USERSPACE->us_textstart &&
98:       (uintptr_t)pc <  (uintptr_t)USERSPACE->us_textend))
99: #else
100:   /* SVCalls are expected only from the base, kernel FLASH region */
101: 
102:   if ((uintptr_t)pc >= (uintptr_t)_stext &&
103:       (uintptr_t)pc <  (uintptr_t)_etext)
104: #endif
105:     {
106:       /* Fetch the instruction that caused the Hard fault */
107: 
108:       uint16_t insn = *pc;
109:       hfinfo("  PC: %p INSN: %04x\n", pc, insn);
110: 
111:       /* If this was the instruction 'svc 0', then forward processing
112:        * to the SVCall handler
113:        */
114: 
115:       if (insn == INSN_SVC0)
116:         {
117:           hfinfo("Forward SVCall\n");
118:           return arm_svcall(irq, context, NULL);
119:         }
120:     }
121: #endif
122: 
123:   if (hfsr & NVIC_HFAULTS_FORCED)
124:     {
125:       hfalert("Hard Fault escalation:\n");
126: #ifdef CONFIG_DEBUG_MEMFAULT
127:       if (cfsr & NVIC_CFAULTS_MEMFAULTSR_MASK)
128:         {
129:           return arm_memfault(irq, context, arg);
130:         }
131: #endif /* CONFIG_DEBUG_MEMFAULT */
132: 
133: #ifdef CONFIG_DEBUG_BUSFAULT
134:       if (cfsr & NVIC_CFAULTS_BUSFAULTSR_MASK)
135:         {
136:           return arm_busfault(irq, context, arg);
137:         }
138: #endif /* CONFIG_DEBUG_BUSFAULT */
139: 
140: #ifdef CONFIG_DEBUG_USAGEFAULT
141:       if (cfsr & NVIC_CFAULTS_USGFAULTSR_MASK)
142:         {
143:           return arm_usagefault(irq, context, arg);
144:         }
145: #endif /* CONFIG_DEBUG_USAGEFAULT */
146: 
147: #ifdef CONFIG_DEBUG_SECUREFAULT
148:       if (sfsr & SAU_SFSR_MASK)
149:         {
150:           return arm_securefault(irq, context, arg);
151:         }
152: #endif /* CONFIG_DEBUG_SECUREFAULT */
153:     }
154: 
155:   /* Dump some hard fault info */
156: 
157:   hfalert("PANIC!!! Hard Fault!:");
158:   hfalert("\tIRQ: %d regs: %p\n", irq, context);
159:   hfalert("\tBASEPRI: %08" PRIx8 " PRIMASK: %08" PRIx8 " IPSR: %08"
160:           PRIx32 " CONTROL: %08" PRIx32 "\n",
161:           getbasepri(), getprimask(), getipsr(), getcontrol());
162:   hfalert("\tCFSR: %08" PRIx32 " HFSR: %08" PRIx32 " DFSR: %08"
163:           PRIx32 " BFAR: %08" PRIx32 " AFSR: %08" PRIx32 "\n",
164:           cfsr, hfsr, getreg32(NVIC_DFAULTS),
165:           getreg32(NVIC_BFAULT_ADDR), getreg32(NVIC_AFAULTS));
166: 
167:   hfalert("Hard Fault Reason:\n");
168: 
169:   if (hfsr & NVIC_HFAULTS_VECTTBL)
170:     {
171:       hfalert("\tBusFault on a vector table read\n");
172:     }
173:   else if (hfsr & NVIC_HFAULTS_DEBUGEVT)
174:     {
175:       hfalert("\tDebug event\n");
176:     }
177: 
178: #ifdef CONFIG_DEBUG_HARDFAULT_ALERT
179:   if (arm_gen_nonsecurefault(irq, context))
180:     {
181:       return OK;
182:     }
183: #endif
184: 
185:   up_irq_save();
186:   PANIC_WITH_REGS("panic", context);
187:   return OK;
188: }

63: void nxsched_process_delivered(int cpu)
64: {
65:   enum task_deliver_e priority;
66:   irqstate_t flags;

68:   DEBUGASSERT(up_interrupt_context());

70:   flags = enter_critical_section();
71:   priority = per_cpu_var_smp(g_delivertasks, cpu);
72:   per_cpu_var_smp(g_delivertasks, cpu) = SWITCH_NONE;

74:   if (priority != SWITCH_NONE &&

42: /****************************************************************************
43:  * Name: nxsched_set_affinity
44:  *
45:  * Description:
46:  *   sched_setaffinity() sets the CPU affinity mask of the thread whose ID
47:  *   is pid to the value specified by mask.  If pid is zero, then the
48:  *   calling thread is used.  The argument cpusetsize is the length (i
49:  *   bytes) of the data pointed to by mask.  Normally this argument would
50:  *   be specified as sizeof(cpu_set_t).
51:  *
52:  *   If the thread specified by pid is not currently running on one of the
53:  *   CPUs specified in mask, then that thread is migrated to one of the
54:  *   CPUs specified in mask.
55:  *
56:  *   nxsched_set_affinity() is identical to the function sched_setparam(),
57:  *   differing only in its return value:  This function does not modify
58:  *   the errno variable.  This is a non-standard, internal OS function and
59:  *   is not intended for use by application logic.  Applications should
60:  *   use the standard sched_setparam().
61:  *
62:  * Input Parameters:
63:  *   pid        - The ID of thread whose affinity set will be modified.
64:  *   cpusetsize - Size of mask.  MUST be sizeofcpu_set_t().
65:  *   mask       - The location to return the thread's new affinity set.
66:  *
67:  * Returned Value:
68:  *   Zero (OK) if successful.  Otherwise, a negated errno value is returned:
69:  *
70:  *     ESRCH  The task whose ID is pid could not be found.
71:  *
72:  ****************************************************************************/
73: 
74: int nxsched_set_affinity(pid_t pid, size_t cpusetsize,
75:                          FAR const cpu_set_t *mask)
76: {
77:   FAR struct tcb_s *tcb;
78:   irqstate_t flags;
79:   int ret = OK;
80: 
81:   DEBUGASSERT(cpusetsize == sizeof(cpu_set_t) && mask != NULL);
82: 
83:   /* Make sure that affinity mask is valid */
84: 
85:   if (*mask == 0)
86:     {
87:       return -EINVAL;
88:     }
89: 
90:   /* Verify that the PID corresponds to a real task */
91: 
92:   if (!pid)
93:     {
94:       tcb = this_task();
95:     }
96:   else
97:     {
98:       tcb = nxsched_get_tcb(pid);
99:     }
100: 
101:   if (tcb == NULL)
102:     {
103:       ret = -ESRCH;
104:       goto errout;
105:     }
106: 
107:   /* Don't permit changing the affinity mask of any task locked to a CPU
108:    * (i.e., an IDLE task)
109:    */
110: 
111:   flags = enter_critical_section();
112:   if ((atomic_read(&tcb->flags) & TCB_FLAG_CPU_LOCKED) != 0)
113:     {
114:       ret = -EINVAL;
115:       goto errout_with_csection;
116:     }
117: 
118:   /* Set the new affinity mask. */
119: 
120:   tcb->affinity = *mask;
121: 
122:   /* Is the task still executing a a CPU in its affinity mask? Will this
123:    * change cause the task to be removed from its current assigned task
124:    * list?
125:    *
126:    * First... is the task in an assigned task list?
127:    */
128: 
129:   if (tcb->task_state >= FIRST_READY_TO_RUN_STATE &&
130:       tcb->task_state <= LAST_READY_TO_RUN_STATE)
131:     {
132:       /* Yes... is the CPU associated with the assigned task in the new
133:        * affinity mask?
134:        */
135: 
136:       if ((tcb->affinity & (1 << tcb->cpu)) == 0)
137:         {
138:           /* No.. then we will need to move the task from the assigned
139:            * task list to some other ready to run list.
140:            *
141:            * nxsched_set_priority() will do just what we want... it will
142:            * remove the task from its current position in the some assigned
143:            * task list and then simply put it back in the right place.  This
144:            * works even if the task is this task.
145:            */
146: 
147:           ret = nxsched_set_priority(tcb, tcb->sched_priority);
148:         }
149:     }
150: 
151: errout_with_csection:
152:   leave_critical_section(flags);
153:   if (pid)
154:     {
155:       nxsched_put_tcb(tcb);
156:     }
157: 
158: errout:
159:   return ret;
160: }

169:  *   bytes) of the data pointed to by mask.  Normally this argument would

1: # BK7258 OpenVela AP移植
2: 
3: 本项目将OpenVela/NuttX移植到BK7258 AP核，并保留博通原厂CP固件、Bootloader、分区和最终打包流程。当前已实现AP核启动，以及AP日志通过Mailbox转发到CP UART0输出。
4: 
5: ## 简单使用说明
6: 
7: 本项目需要配合博通`bk_avdk_smp` SMP工程使用：
8: 
9: ```text
10: 工作区/
11: ├── contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/
12: └── bk_avdk_smp/
13: ```
14: 
15: 构建前，需要将比赛仓`external/bk_avdk_smp/`中的权威覆盖文件同步到
16: `bk_avdk_smp`。完整文件清单、可直接执行的同步脚本、逐字节校验、OpenVela AP
17: 构建、CP构建和最终固件打包步骤见`external/bk_avdk_smp/README.md`。Git协作和
18: 提交规则见`github开发指南.md`。
19: 
20: ## UART0控制台使用
21: 
22: 连接开发板UART0：
23: 
24: ```bash
25: picocom --no-escape -b 115200 --flow n --parity n --databits 8 /dev/ttyUSB0
26: ```
27: 
28: CP启动后可先查看AP链路状态，再进入AP的OpenVela NSH控制台：
29: 
30: ```text
31: ap_console status
32: ap_console open
33: ```
34: 
35: 进入AP控制台后可以直接执行NSH命令，例如：
36: 
37: ```text
38: help
39: uname -a
40: ps
41: free
42: ctrlc_test
43: ```
44: 
45: `ctrlc_test`会持续等待TTY `SIGINT`。按`Ctrl-C`后应打印
46: `ctrlc_test received SIGINT`并返回NSH提示符。
47: 
48: AP控制台支持方向键、Home、End、Delete、Backspace、命令历史，以及
49: `Ctrl-A`、`Ctrl-B`、`Ctrl-D`、`Ctrl-E`、`Ctrl-F`、`Ctrl-H`、`Ctrl-K`、
50: `Ctrl-L`、`Ctrl-N`、`Ctrl-P`和`Ctrl-U`等CLE快捷键。
51: 
52: 退出AP控制台并返回CP命令行时，严格按以下顺序操作：
53: 
54: 1. 按下`Ctrl-]`。
55: 2. 松开按键。
56: 3. 再按`.`。
57: 
58: 返回CP命令行后可再次检查状态：
59: 
60: ```text
61: ap_console status
62: ```
63: 
64: ## 主要目录
65: 
66: ```text
67: board/beken/chips/bk7258/                  BK7258 AP启动、中断、定时器和Mailbox驱动
68: board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/       BK7258 AP板级配置、链接脚本和bring-up
69: external/bk_avdk_smp/                      已验证的博通CP覆盖文件
70: logs/                                      AI Coding日志
71: ```
72: 
73: ## 已实现功能
74: 
75: - BK7258物理CPU1/AP启动OpenVela/NuttX。
76: - Cortex-M33启动向量、C运行时、MPU、FPU、IRQ和SysTick基础适配。
77: - Mailbox v2基础传输、logical channel、sequence、ACK、超时和FIFO full恢复。
78: - 原厂兼容HW_CTRL command 1 power-up、command 2两秒heartbeat，以及独立的PWC `0x5/0x11`生命周期握手。
79: - AP日志通过Mailbox UART0转发到CP物理UART0。
80: - GPIO40红灯和GPIO41绿灯由NuttX内核自动LED状态接口接管，用于显示
81:   中断、信号、断言、Panic、空闲和启动状态。
82: - AP、CP和Bootloader通过`bk_avdk_smp`标准打包流程生成`all-app.bin`。
83: - 当前为物理CPU1+CPU2的OpenVela/NuttX SMP，CP保持物理CPU0。
84:

213: 
214:       ret = data->func(data->arg);

216:       flags = spin_lock_irqsave(&g_smp_call_lock);
217: 
218:       cookie = data->cookie;

58: void nxsched_unlock(FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb)
59: {
60:   irqstate_t flags = enter_critical_section();
61:   FAR struct tcb_s *ptcb;
62: 
63:   /* In non-SMP:
64:    * If lockcount equals 0 and interrupts are not masked,
65:    * an interrupt may occur just before processing the g_pendingtasks queue,
66:    * causing the scheduler to switch to and start executing a lower-priority
67:    * task. At this moment, if there is a higher-priority task in the
68:    * g_pendingtasks queue, priority inversion will occur.
69:    */
70: 
71:   rtcb->lockcount = 0;
72: 
73:   /* Note that we no longer have pre-emption disabled. */
74: 
75:   if (!up_interrupt_context())
76:     {
77:       nxsched_critmon_preemption(rtcb, false, return_address(0));
78:       sched_note_preemption(rtcb, false);
79:     }
80: 
81:   /* Release any ready-to-run tasks that have collected in
82:    * g_pendingtasks.
83:    *
84:    * NOTE: This operation has a very high likelihood of causing
85:    * this task to be switched out!
86:    */
87: 
88: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
89:   ptcb = (FAR struct tcb_s *)dq_peek(list_readytorun());
90:   if (ptcb && ptcb->sched_priority > rtcb->sched_priority &&
91:       nxsched_deliver_task(rtcb->cpu, rtcb->cpu, SWITCH_HIGHER))
92: #else
93:   ptcb = (FAR struct tcb_s *)dq_peek(list_pendingtasks());
94:   if (ptcb && nxsched_merge_pending())
95: #endif
96:     {
97:       nxsched_switch(this_task(), rtcb);
98:     }
99: 
100: #if CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL > 0
101:   /* If (1) the task that was running supported round-robin
102:    * scheduling and (2) if its time slice has already expired, but
103:    * (3) it could not slice out because pre-emption was disabled,
104:    * then we need to swap the task out now and reassess the interval
105:    * timer for the next time slice.
106:    */
107: 
108:   if ((atomic_read(&rtcb->flags) & TCB_FLAG_POLICY_MASK) ==
109:       TCB_FLAG_SCHED_RR && rtcb->timeslice == 0)
110:     {
111:       /* Yes.. that is the situation.  But one more thing.  The call
112:        * to nxsched_merge_pending() above may have actually replaced
113:        * the task at the head of the ready-to-run list.  In that
114:        * case, we need only to reset the timeslice value back to the
115:        * maximum.
116:        */
117: 
118:       if (rtcb != this_task())
119:         {
120:           rtcb->timeslice = MSEC2TICK(CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL);
121:         }
122: #  ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_TICKLESS
123:       else if ((atomic_or(&rtcb->flags, TCB_FLAG_PREEMPT_SCHED) &
124:                 TCB_FLAG_PREEMPT_SCHED) == 0)
125:         {
126:           nxsched_reassess_timer();
127:           atomic_and(&rtcb->flags, ~TCB_FLAG_PREEMPT_SCHED);
128:         }
129: #  endif
130:     }

text:
**Conclusion**

The strongest root cause is a boot-handshake race: `BOOT_ACK` is transmitted from inside CPU1’s first mailbox ISR, but CPU0 interprets it as proof that CPU1 has completed exception return and is scheduler-ready. It has not. CPU0 can finish `up_cpu_start()` and expose CPU1 to normal scheduling/SMP-call traffic while CPU1 is still between the mailbox callback and the first Thread-mode instruction after `cpsie i`.

There is also a real Cortex-M33 FPU initialization defect: neither AP core calls `arm_fpuconfig()`. It is especially dangerous on CPU1 because its first FP instruction is the unconditional `vmsr fpscr` in `exception_direct`, executed during this first mailbox exception.

**Root-Cause Candidates**

1. **Premature ACK makes CPU0 release the secondary before exception return**  
   **Confidence: high, approximately 85%.**

   CPU1 enables interrupts at [bk7258_cpustart.c:67](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_cpustart.c:67). The pending mailbox IRQ can preempt immediately inside `up_irq_enable()`, before stage 9 is written. The ACK is sent and stage 10 is written inside that IRQ at [bk7258_smpcall.c:137](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_smpcall.c:137).

   CPU0 considers `NOTIFY|ACK` complete at [bk7258_smpcall.c:246](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_smpcall.c:246), then returns from `up_cpu_start()` at [bk7258_cpustart.c:234](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_cpustart.c:234). CPU1 does not publish stages 11/12 until after the IRQ has returned at [bk7258_cpustart.c:68](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_cpustart.c:68).

   Immediately after `nx_smp_start()`, NuttX starts creating runnable tasks at [nx_start.c:805](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/init/nx_start.c:805). Remote task delivery sends a scheduling IPI at [sched.h:489](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/sched/sched.h:489), and an SMP-call IPI executes arbitrary callbacks directly in IRQ context at [sched_smp.c:191](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/sched/sched_smp.c:191). The latter bypasses CPU1 idle’s initial scheduler lock.

   The repository’s hardware history records this exact regression after early affinity/SMP-call activity, and records success after suppressing those operations until stage 12: [external README.md:694](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/external/bk_avdk_smp/README.md:694).

   The current `wait_secondary_scheduler()` at [bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:172](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:172) is only a late worker-level workaround. It runs after `up_cpu_start()` has already returned, so it does not repair the architecture contract.

2. **CPU1 lacks mandatory per-core FPU setup, creating an EXC_RETURN/lazy-stacking hazard**  
   **Confidence: medium-high, approximately 65%.**

   `bk7258_cpu_private_initialize()` grants CP10/CP11 access but does not set `CONTROL.FPCA` or disable lazy FP stacking: [bk7258_start.c:107](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_start.c:107). Neither the primary nor secondary path calls `arm_fpuconfig()`.

   The first external IRQ enters `exception_direct`, which unconditionally executes `vmsr fpscr` at [arm_doirq.c:46](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/arch/arm/src/armv8-m/arm_doirq.c:46). On CPU1 this is plausibly its first FP instruction after reset, with `CONTROL.FPCA=0` and reset/default `FPCCR.ASPEN/LSPEN`.

   NuttX’s intended setup explicitly sets FPCA and disables lazy stacking at [arm_fpuconfig.c:57](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/arch/arm/src/armv8-m/arm_fpuconfig.c:57). The common exception assembly then relies on EXC_RETURN bit 4 to choose the FP frame layout at [arm_exception.S:172](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/arch/arm/src/arm_m/arm_exception.S:172) and [arm_exception.S:289](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/arch/arm/src/arm_m/arm_exception.S:289).

   A working Cortex-M SMP port initializes the interrupt stack, NVIC, and then FPU independently on every secondary core before enabling its IPI: [cxd56_cpustart.c:100](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/arch/arm/src/cxd56xx/cxd56_cpustart.c:100).

   Expected failure signatures are `CFSR.INVPC`, `LSPERR`, `MLSPERR`, `UNSTKERR`, or `STKOF`. This defect is independently worth fixing even if candidate 1 is the trigger.

3. **Stage 10 is not monotonic and can be written again by a stale or duplicate BOOT_PING**  
   **Confidence: medium, approximately 45%.**

   Every `BOOT_PING` unconditionally writes stage 10, regardless of whether CPU1 previously reached stage 12 or 13: [bk7258_smpcall.c:137](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_smpcall.c:137). Therefore `secondary=10` alone does not prove CPU1 never returned.

   The mailbox initialization intentionally preserves pre-existing FIFO entries at [bk7258_mbox0.c:397](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mbox0.c:397), while secondary initialization only clears error status and enables the route at [bk7258_mbox0.c:440](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mbox0.c:440). An AP-only reset can therefore leave diagnostic ambiguity.

   A single ISR cannot drain forever because it has an eight-entry budget at [bk7258_mbox0.c:233](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mbox0.c:233).
